messages:

Cc: lisa.chen@brightwavehealth.com
Date: 2026-04-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluation kickoff: outline for success gates and timeline

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Leadership wants a short, actionable mutual plan we can sign off on that spells out: success criteria, what counts as a pass/fail for the pilot, and the close timeline if things look good. We have a 6-week evaluation window budgeted.

High level asks from BrightWave:
- Clear acceptance tests (functional + performance) for core use case (claims summarization).
- Security/compliance checklist we can hand to procurement (SOC2 evidence, data retention options).
- A short fallback plan if quality falls below threshold (model downgrade/latency tradeoff).

Can you send a proposed MAP + acceptance-test matrix by EOD Wednesday? That will let us prep internal reviewers.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Reddy
Head of Data Platforms, BrightWave Health
[Attachment: none]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@brightwavehealth.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-21T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation kickoff: outline for success gates and timeline

Sanjay — thanks, this is helpful context. Attached is our proposed MAP and an acceptance test matrix (attached): MAP_draft_v2.pdf and acceptance_test_matrix.xlsx. Summary below of the critical success checks we recommend for the 6-week sprint.

Proposed critical success checks (high-level):
1) Functional correctness (claims summarization) — Acceptance: F1 >= 0.78 on benchmark set + manual review pass rate >= 85% on 200 clinical samples.
2) Determinism / safety — No high-severity hallucinations in spot checks (0 in 250 samples), and redaction of PHI fields meets spec.
3) Latency & throughput — 95th percentile latency <= 750ms for 1-2 concurrent users during peak testing; sustained throughput of 10 rps for batch runs.
4) Cost target — per-claim inference cost <= $0.015 with recommended batching and kv-cache settings.
5) Integration stability — SDK/endpoint error rate < 0.5% over the evaluation window.

Exit gates (what constitutes a pass to move to pilot close):
- All high-priority functional tests pass OR documented compensating mitigation and timeline for fixes (canary for fixes).
- Compliance checklist items flagged as "needs info" must have owners and due dates.
- Mutual signoff on go/no-go 48 hours after final smoke run.

Acceptance tests (examples from matrix):
- Automated evaluation: thresholded F1/ROUGE on labeled set (details in spreadsheet).
- Human review: 200-sample round, scoring rubric attached.
- Performance: scripted load test capturing p95/p99 latency and token cost.
- Security: SOC2 artifact list + retention config check (see section 3 of MAP).

Proposed timeline (6-week):
Week 0 (kickoff): MAP signoff, share test data and sandbox creds.
Week 1-2: Integration + smoke tests.
Week 3-4: Full evaluation runs (automated + human sample).
Week 5: Remediation window (if needed) + final run.
Week 6: Final smoke, mutual signoff, go/no-go.

Action items I propose now:
- You: confirm owners for compliance items and whether you need an on-site security review.
- We: run the first integration smoke by EOD next Wednesday.

Attaching: MAP_draft_v2.pdf (draft MAP), acceptance_test_matrix.xlsx (test details).

Thanks — can loop in Monica for compliance specifics (cc'd).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_draft_v2.pdf (application/pdf), acceptance_test_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Sanjay / team — quick compliance and operational notes from my side after skimming the draft MAP:

1) SOC2 & evidence: we'll provide the SOC2 Type II report and a one-pager mapping BrightWave's questions to the artifacts. We'll also list the endpoints where audit logs are emitted and retention windows.

2) Data handling: for the evaluation we can use a dedicated sandbox with configurable retention (default 30 days). If you need shorter retention we can scope that into the MAP; will need an order form addendum for Dedicated controls.

3) Acceptance-test additions: recommend adding a security smoke checklist to be run before human review — includes redaction verification, access control checks, and one authenticated replay of a sampled request ledger.

4) Fallback plan: propose a model variant gating policy in the MAP: if manual-review precision drops below 75% for two consecutive days, autoswitch to quantized smaller model for reads-only / safe-mode and flag for urgent fix. Jordan — can you capture the operational runbook snippet and the rollback command set?

I'll drop a short compliance appendix to the MAP by EOD that enumerates artifact names and owners.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

1) Can you add expected data retention behavior for sandbox logs explicitly in section 3 (30-day default, optional 7-day setting — we prefer 7 days if possible)?
2) For the fallback flow, please include the exact SDK flag we need to set in our staging infra to force the quantized model — that will help our SRE run a pre-mortem.

If you can add those two pieces and re-issue the MAP, I can circulate to procurement and sign the mutual plan next Tuesday. Attaching a signed stub we use for internal tracking (signed_map_stub.pdf) — procurement will still need the SOC2 artifact but this gives them the go-ahead.
